name: J. C. Fisher
role: Medora businessman, postmaster, stage line manager and Republican leader
bio: J. C. Fisher was a Medora businessman and Republican organizer who chaired the county central committee in 1884. In August 1884 he became local manager of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., and that fall he built two stores on Third Avenue and talked of adding a roller rink. By January 1885 he was signing the post office's unclaimed-letter lists as postmaster, and with Rassie Deffebach he ran the roller rink, where he also kept a shooting gallery and fitted up the post office. He chaired the December 1884 school meeting, served as a school trustee in 1885, and rode out to the E6 ranch and Wadsworth's beef round-up that year. He appeared on the Stockmen's Ticket in March 1886, and in December 1886 he left to spend a month or more in Elyria, Ohio.
